Celebrate Mother’s Day with an afternoon of creativity, connection, and indulgence at our special succulent arranging workshop. Treat yourself and the moms in your life to a unique experience that blends nature, artistry, and a touch of sweetness. 
Guided by an expert succulent designer, you’ll learn tips for succulent care and styling before diving into the hands-on creation of a vibrant succulent arrangement. 
Design your masterpiece in a charming hand-made heart-shaped planter, perfect for adding a splash of color and personality to any space. All materials, including premium succulents, specialty soil, and care cards, are provided—so you can focus on making memories and crafting a one-of-a-kind piece. 
Snack on some tea and beautiful floral cookies and leave with a beautiful creation and cherished moments to treasure. 
Sunday, May 10 from 3 to 4 p.m. 
Public $80, TBG Members $75 (plus applicable taxes and fees). 
About Canadian Succulents 
Canadian Succulents is a small business that creates floral arrangements using entirely succulents and cacti plants. They not only arrange and design all of the creations but also grow all the plants that can be found in them as well. They operate out of a greenhouse just north east of the city, where they grow over 300 varieties of succulents and cacti. They grow and create these designs for wedding centrepieces and favors, corporate events and gifting, and hotel and office greenery. 
http://www.canadiansucculents.net/ 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member! 
Additional Program Information 

Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: Create Hip-Hop Music with AI Tools for Teens
description:
Have you ever had a melody stuck in your head and wished you could turn it into a real song? AI tools are making it easier than ever to bring your musical experiences to life - but how do you make sure the music you create is truly yours?
Explore how to use AI as a creative assistant to build radio-ready hip-hop tracks based on your own original ideas. You'll learn how to guide AI tools to serve your vision rather than replace it, and we'll cover Canadian copyright guidelines to ensure the music you make qualifies as your own intellectual property. No prior music or programming experience is required.
This program is part of the Innovator in Residence (AI and Music Production) program, which is designed to help beginner and intermediate learners build knowledge and creative skills and get hands-on with current AI tools in music production and learn about the history, copyright and ethics of generative music. For more information and a full list of programs, visit
tpl.ca/airesident
.

title: Adopting GitHub in the Enterprise: Best Practices and Strategies
description:
Toronto Enterprise DevOps User Group
Adopting GitHub in an enterprise environment can significantly enhance collaboration, streamline workflows, and improve code quality. However, successful adoption requires careful planning and implementation of best practices. This presentation will cover key strategies for integrating GitHub into your organization's development processes. We will discuss topics such as setting up repositories, managing access controls, implementing branching strategies, and leveraging GitHub Actions for CI/CD. Additionally, we will explore how to foster a culture of collaboration through code reviews and issue tracking. Attendees will gain insights into overcoming common challenges and ensuring a smooth transition to GitHub, ultimately driving productivity and innovation within their teams.

Key topics covered:

* Setting up single sign-on (SSO) and integrating with existing identity providers
* Configuring Enterprise Account settings and policies
* Organization structure and repository management
* Managing user access and permissions effectively
* Hybrid Model for GitHub and Azure DevOps
* Securing GitHub Actions and workflows
* Implementing shift-left security practices
* Addressing security concerns and ensuring data protection
* Rolling out GitHub Copilot in an enterprise setting
* Leveraging GitHub Apps and integrations for enhanced functionality
* Integrating GitHub with existing development tools and systems
* Monitoring and auditing usage for compliance

*Come at 5:30 pm have some pizza and chat for a bit. The presentation starts at 6:00 pm.*

title: Bees: A Story of Survival
location: Royal Ontario Museum, 100 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C6
description:
Bringing some buzz into your summer.

Journey into the world of bees in a stunning new immersive experience that brings together the beauty of art with the power of science. Created by the National Museums Liverpool in partnership with award-winning artist and sculptor, Wolfgang Buttress, the exhibition highlights 120-million years of bee adaptation and survival, telling the epic tale of these incredible creatures and their relationship to us and the natural world.

Based on science and full of imagination, the experiential exhibition presents a fusion of nature, art, music, and architecture that transports visitors into the world of bees - from the tiny, fascinating anatomy of a single bee and the magical wonder of honey bee colonies to the important roles bees play in our lives and the everyday threats they face.

Through immersive environments, art installations, soundscapes, and more, learn about the life of bees and the world they inhabit.

title: Her Smoke Rose Up Forever - James Tiptree Jr.
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi all,

For May, we will be reading another short story collection. Following April’s selection, *Best American Science Fiction and Fantasy 2025*, we’ll turn to an older anthology. This collection features stories by a science fiction writer who remained cloaked in mystery for years.

Book of the Month
*Her Smoke Rose Up Forever* \- James Tiptree Jr\. \(1990\)

Direct from [this amazing Portalist](https://theportalist.com/james-tiptree-jr-enigmatic-author) article:
"James Tiptree Jr. left an enduring mark on modern speculative fiction — but she’s perhaps more mysterious and enigmatic today than ever before.

Tiptree was one of the pen names used by female sci-fi author Alice Bradley Sheldon (née Alice Hastings Bradley). The daughter of prolific fiction writer Mary Hastings Bradley, Sheldon may have been born with the gift of words, but her path to literary success wasn’t clear-cut.

Although Sheldon is best known for her sci-fi writing, she had an eclectic and accomplished career. At various times in her life, Sheldon was a research psychologist, painter, art critic, imagery intelligence operative, CIA operative, and more. In many of these fields, she was one of the few women in an industry dominated by men. "

Given this and Tiptree's well-known stories included in this collection, I don't think we can pass up this opportunity. As with any other collection we read for Book Club, if a story isn't speaking to you, go ahead and skip it! There are 18 selections in here, I'm sure we'll have plenty to discuss.

Below, you'll find a few notables and a brief description:

* “The Women Men Don’t See” – A classic feminist sci-fi story exploring gender, invisibility, and societal expectations.
* “Houston, Houston, Do You Read?” – A Hugo Award–winning story about time travel, gender, and post-apocalyptic society.
* “Love Is the Plan the Plan Is Death” – A highly acclaimed story told from the perspective of an alien species, exploring instinct, love, and survival.
* “The Girl Who Was Plugged In” – A groundbreaking cyberpunk-like story about identity, media, and corporate control of bodies.
* “And I Awoke and Found Me Here on the Cold Hill’s Side” – A dark, unsettling exploration of obsession and desire for alien contact.

There are a few printings of this collections. I think [I'm going to pick up this one](https://bookshop.org/p/books/her-smoke-rose-up-forever-james-tiptree/163a6a04d0124023?ean=9781892391209&next=t&utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=%7Bcampaignname%7D&utm_content=6443417794&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=16235479093&gbraid=0AAAAACfld43fka72FJRQfybRz8siTTDOZ&gclid=Cj0KCQiAprLLBhCMARIsAEDhdPdhUhUk1aiXVGaWtVIu9frZcido-IwCeX0rcqajtxQRQLphaxpwy68aAvCqEALw_wcB), as it includes some revisions from the author’s original notes.

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/MM3hNQFW). Join us and keep the conversation going.

title: Penderecki Quartet 40th Anniversary Concert
location: Jane Mallett Theatre, St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts, 27 Front St E, Toronto, ON, M5E 1B4
description:
Their journey began in Poland, where they won the prestigious Penderecki Prize at the 1986 National Chamber Music Competition in Łódź. 

Since 1991, they have served as Quartet-in-Residence at Wilfrid Laurier University, helping shape one of Canada’s premier string programs. Known for their dedication to contemporary music, the Penderecki’s have commissioned and performed over 100 new works. 

We invite you to enjoy their program of Krzysztof Penderecki: String Quartet No. 3 Leaves of an Unwritten Diary and Franz Schubert: Quintet in C major for Two Cellos, D. 956.

Arrive early to enjoy a pre-concert performance by Jacques Forestier, violin. 
Categories: Cultural, Live Performances, Music

title: Hilary Hahn on Violin with Tom Poster on Piano
location: Koerner Hall, Royal Conservatory of Music, 273 Bloor St W, Toronto, ON, M5S 1W2
description:
Three-time Grammy Award-winning violinist Hilary Hahn melds expressive musicality and technical expertise with a diverse repertoire guided by artistic curiosity. She is currently artist-in-residence at both the Chicago Symphony Orchestra and London’s Wigmore Hall, and is co-founder and vice president of artistic partnerships of the AI-music initiative Deepmusic.AI. Hahn is a prolific and celebrated recording artist whose 21 feature albums on Decca, Deutsche Grammophon, and Sony have all opened in the top ten of the Billboard charts.

Enjoy her program of Maurice Ravel: Violin Sonata No. 2 in G Major, M. 77, Bun-Ching Lam: Solitude d’automne, Lili Boulanger: Nocturne, Maurice Ravel: Pièce en forme de Habanera, M. 51, Claude Debussy: Sonata for Violin and Piano in G Minor, Scott Tixier: new duo work (North American premiere), and Gabriel Fauré: Violin Sonata No. 1 in A Major, op. 13.

Categories: Arts/Exhibits, Live Performances, Music

title: Music Copyright and Ethics in the AI Era
description:
When you use AI to create music, who actually owns it? Can a melody generated by a machine infringe on someone else's copyright? As AI tools become more accessible, these questions are more relevant than ever - and the answers aren't always straightforward.
In this session, you'll get a plain-language breakdown of how music copyright works, what the rules are around sampling, and how these long-standing principles apply to AI-generated music. You'll also hear about landmark legal cases - both surprising victories and cautionary tales - including real-world examples from a working composer's own career.
Drop-in. No registration required.
This program is part of the Innovator in Residence (AI and Music Production) program, which is designed to help beginner and intermediate learners build knowledge and creative skills and get hands-on with current AI tools in music production and learn about the history, copyright and ethics of generative music. For more information and a full list of programs, visit
tpl.ca/airesident
.

title: Japanese Tea Ceremony
description:
Experience the traditional art of the Japanese tea ceremony.  Learn about Japanese culture and the important philosophy behind the tea ceremony. This presentation not only offers a demonstration of traditional Matcha preparation using authentic tools, but zen philosophies which may also apply to daily life. Discover how Matcha is harvested, its history, how to make/use it, how to differenciate between different grades, and how to conserve it.
Reina Sakao is a fourth-generation tea house and Urasenke tea instructor who trained at the Urasenke School in Japan where her family owns and operates a tea plantation in Shizuoka. Reina has over 10 years of experience with the Japanese tea ceremony (first-degree Urasenke tea ceremony instructor).​

Post-Apocalyptic Book Club - Toronto Chapter
This time we'll be reading Roadside Picnic by Arkady and Boris Strugatsky. Here's the blurb:

Red Schuhart is a stalker, one of those young rebels who are compelled, in spite of extreme danger, to venture illegally into the Zone to collect the mysterious artifacts that the alien visitors left scattered around. His life is dominated by the place and the thriving black market in the alien products. But when he and his friend Kirill go into the Zone together to pick up a “full empty,” something goes wrong. And the news he gets from his girlfriend upon his return makes it inevitable that he’ll keep going back to the Zone, again and again, until he finds the answer to all his problems.

First published in 1972, *Roadside Picnic* is still widely regarded as one of the greatest science fiction novels.

title: Prepare The Ground 2026
location: Trinity St Paul's, 427 Bloor St W, Toronto, ON, M5S 1X7
description:
A community-led arts and heavy music festival, the first of its kind in the city! 

Founded by two lifelong friends, Toronto-based concert promoter Denholm Whale and KW Campol of music management company Mythos and the Perpetual Flame Ministries record label/art house. 

Drawing inspiration from European festival stalwarts like Roadburn, Supersonic, and Amplifest, we're focused on heavy music as an ethos of collective catharsis more than a dedication to one specific metal subgenre. From burgeoning artists, to favorites you never thought would reunite, to one-off full album sets, a heavily curated and meticulously planned lineup is the festival’s key component.

title: OTTAWA: Culture in the Capital    (8th annual visit)
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
Can you join us in **Ottawa**?

*For our annual culture long weekend! **Our 8th year.***

Dates/details are now FIRM--thinking about early summer Culture!

PLEASE read everything over before signing up--all the details are here.

As optimism builds for a different year (more comfortable) in 2026 then we had in previous years--we will continue to explore the culture scene in some of our favorite Cities. **A deep dive/below the surface.**

Each year we bounce back and forth between Montreal & Ottawa.

This year in Ottawa--we'll also spend some time in **GATINEAU** for the first time--we can ***WALK*** between downtown Ottawa and downtown Gatineau (it takes just 30 minutes!!)

This will be our 8th 'long weekend' Ottawa trip since 2015. (--not the sleepy city you think it is--)

**Very important, PLEASE read all the information over before you RSVP.**

**You must contact me first. There is a *Non-Refundable fee* to join us. Emailed/payable when you are confirmed. $100 per person**

**Our 2026 Ottawa trip will be built around**--our favorite contemporary galleries, architecture, public art, The National Gallery, and its **Doors Open Ottawa** weekend +++ food/drink

**Plus our other usual favorite stops,** and a Group dinner.

All in 2 1/2 days!!

We are on the go each day from 10:30am-9pm, and **walk** everywhere.

Ottawa is the least expensive of our trips--perhaps $1000 all in?

What else do we do? Some combo of:

-visit other private/public galleries
-architecture tour/talks/walks
-Indigenous exploration
-public outdoor art
-food/drink
-other things which we don't yet know about
-much of what we do is FREE

**Note:** there is so much going on in Ottawa with regards to ART and CULTURE--don't think otherwise! We are welcomed everywhere.

This is a 3-night trip. The dates of this trip are AFTER the Ottawa Tulip Festival.

**How these trips work:**

**YOU look after** your travel and accommodations (everyone has own personal budgets), **I look after** everything else. I plan ALL our activities on the ground while we are together. From first night drink/gallery visit (Thursday), to last night's group dinner (Saturday). You leave as you like on Sunday.

1. 3 nights (Thursday, Friday, Saturday) We meet as a group on Thursday at 5pm SHARP.
2. VIA train is currently showing $150 round trip ticket. How will you get there, where will you stay? Drive, bus, train, fly? (Your Presto card works in Ottawa--on public transit!)
3. Will you drive your car? Use 'points' for accommodations? Airbnb, B&B, Hotel, other? Do you need any insurance? You should aim to stay within a 15 mins walk of downtown/Byward Market. We walk everywhere!
4. There is a **NON-refundable fee sent to me when you signup/RSVP--due within 2 days.** I organize everything on the ground, discounts, tours, reservations etc. **TRIP FEE for 2026 is $100 per person.**
5. We will start with 10 people..until we know more about group sizing. But no more than 12 people.
6. Build into your trip budget: $75 for tickets/tours/entry, and $125 for our famous last night **group dinner**--we always find someplace special/memorable. Excellent OTTAWA food scene.
7. And of course, with all our trips there are always special/vip type surprises.
8. Agenda/schedule/Details in due course. You want to be in Ottawa and able to MEET up by **5pm on Thursday June 4th**. At the National Gallery.

Please read everything over before signing up. I keep you in the loop as per our planning, with a final schedule sent to you a few weeks before.

Thank you for your interest!

You can connect with me (Greg) at
[torontoisculture@gmail.com](http://torontoisculture@gmail.com/)

On **Saturday June 6th**, **let's Celebrate 50 Years of Magic with Penn & Teller.** Penn & Teller return to Toronto for the first time in 16 years with an unforgettable night of mind-blowing illusions, sharp wit, and legendary showmanship. Penn & Teller are a legendary magic act - Emmy, Obie, and Writer’s Guild Award-winning, with stars on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Penn & Teller know magic. Their CW TV show “Penn & Teller: Fool Us” has launched countless magic careers, while successful Broadway runs and sold-out overseas tours have secured their place in the history books. title: Create Pop Music with AI Tools for Teens
description:
Have you ever had a melody stuck in your head and wished you could turn it into a real song? AI tools are making it easier than ever to bring your musical experiences to life - but how do you make sure the music you create is truly yours?
Explore how to use AI as a creative assistant to build radio-ready pop tracks based on your own original ideas. You'll learn how to guide AI tools to serve your vision rather than replace it, and we'll cover Canadian copyright guidelines to ensure the music you make qualifies as your own intellectual property. No prior musical experience is required.
This program is for teens. Registration is required.
This program is part of the Innovator in Residence (AI and Music Production) program, which is designed to help beginner and intermediate learners build knowledge and creative skills and get hands-on with current AI tools in music production and learn about the history, copyright and ethics of generative music. title: Music Copyright and Ethics in the AI Era
description:
When you use AI to create music, who actually owns it? Can a melody generated by a machine infringe on someone else's copyright? As AI tools become more accessible, these questions are more relevant than ever - and the answers aren't always straightforward.
In this session, you'll get a plain-language breakdown of how music copyright works, what the rules are around sampling, and how these long-standing principles apply to AI-generated music. You'll also hear about landmark legal cases - both surprising victories and cautionary tales - including real-world examples from a working composer's own career.
Drop-in, no registration required.
This program is part of the Innovator in Residence (AI and Music Production) program, which is designed to help beginner and intermediate learners build knowledge and creative skills and get hands-on with current AI tools in music production and learn about the history, copyright and ethics of generative music. title: 10 Days in a Madhouse
location: Bluma Appel Theatre, 27 Front St E, Toronto, ON, M5E 1B4
description:
Is she insane, or just pretending? 

In this gripping psychological opera based on true events from 1887, trailblazing reporter Nellie Bly fakes madness to expose the truth from inside New York’s notorious Blackwell’s Asylum. What she discovers is a world where women are silenced, sanity is questioned, and power decides who is believed. 

This Canadian premiere from composer Rene Orth and librettist Hannah Moscovitch stars Mireille Asselin as Nellie Bly and Jorell Williams as Dr. Blackwell. 

Directed by Joanna Settle (Sky on Swings), 10 Days in a Madhouse boasts an evocative set by Andrew Lieberman that transforms the asylum into a maze of the mind. Composed by Rene Orth with a libretto by Hannah Moscovitch, 10 Days in a Madhouse is directed by Joanna Settle (Sky on Swings). Designer Andrew Lieberman’s set transforms the asylum into a maze of the mind. 
Categories: Arts/Exhibits, Live Performances, Theatre

title: Los Callejeros Exhibition
location: Assembly Hall Gallery, 1 Colonel Samuel Smith Park Dr, Etobicoke, ON, M8V 4B6
description:
Explore selections from works reflecting Jim Bravo’s memories of his early immigrant inner-city experiences, and correlated interpretations of our sublime Canadian landscape. This exhibition adds yet another voice to the developing story and renewed global interest surrounding questions of race and immigration witnessed in society recently. 

About the Artist 
Jim Bravo was born in Ecuador, South America, and is of Afro-Latino and Quichua descent. He emigrated to Toronto Canada with his family in the mid 70s and spent his youth in the downtown central west and east core of the city. He is a graduate of The Ontario College of Art and Design University where he majored in Fine Art and public monumental painting. A multi award winning painter including first honor for the prestigious 2023 Kingston Prize For Contemporary Canadian Portraiture, Bravo is also the recipient of grants from Toronto Art Council, Ontario Arts Council grants and TABIA Mural Award. 
Categories: Arts/Exhibits, Artisan

title: Play Dead
location: Meridian Arts Centre, 5040 Yonge St, North York, ON, M2N 6R8
description:
Play Dead invites you into a distorted world where the familiar twists into something wonderful and strange. Everyday rituals warp into surreal scenes, exposing the desperation that underpins our search for connection. In this gravity-defying universe, bodies collide and tangle, caught between beauty and menace — both intimate and unsettling.

Montreal’s People Watching crafts a vivid blend of acrobatics, movement, and high octane circus that magnifies the absurdity of the everyday. These moments, strange yet achingly familiar, mirror our own desire to hold on, like couples not wanting the last dance to end.

Haunting and exhilarating, Play Dead captures the fragility, absurdity, and fleeting wonder of life lived on the edge of connection.

La Presse lauds the performance as “Masterful fluidity, breathtaking…the circus of tomorrow".
Categories: Dance, Live Performances

title: Station Eleven - Emily St. John Mandel
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi everyone,

Our novel for June came in at a close second for contemporary picks on our survey. The story takes place around a devastating flu pandemic that threatens society as we know it. It's often cited as one of the more prophetic novels of recent times, but takes things well beyond the covid pandemic.

Book of the Month
*Station Eleven -* Emily St. John Mandel (2014)

From [Grimdark Magazine](https://www.grimdarkmagazine.com/review-station-eleven-by-emily-st-john-mandel/), "*Station Eleven* by Emily St. John Mandel takes the best parts of the dystopian science fiction and fantasy genre and does one thing most books can’t, give the reader hope." I really like the way [A Little Book Problem](https://alittlebookproblem.co.uk/2023/08/04/book-review-station-eleven-by-emily-st-john-mandel-book-6-of-20booksofsummer/#:~:text=The%20book%20is%20a%20beautiful%2C,to%20in%20a%20world%20when)'s review describes the tone. "The book is a beautiful, heart-wrenching and moving exploration of what is important to us in life, what we would hang on to in a world when almost everything we know and care about is torn away, and what kind of people we discover we are in the face of great adversity."

*Station Eleven* shows how science fiction isn’t just about the future. It’s about how we live today, and the threads that connect us all. It's a celebration of the arts and bound to be a great conversation. I look forward to discussing this one with you!

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/B9NMnC2F). Join us and keep the conversation going.

title: Industry Registration - 2026 CRAFT Microfluidics Professional Course
location: Bahen Centre, 40 St. George Street, Toronto, Canada
description:
The Microfluidics Professional Course is a 3-day crash course for industrial/academic researchers with little or no experience in the microfluidics field. Led by our expert staff, and utilizing our state of the art cleanroom facility, labs will cover various fabrication techniques including prototyping of polymer devices using lithography and 3D printing, and small scale-up fabrication of thermoplastic devices for commercialization using injection molding and roll-2-roll coating.In our CL2 bio facilities we will cover cell/tissue culture techniques and advanced imaging for validating and carrying out MF experiments. At the end of the course you will have been exposed to a variety of the latest research being carried out using MF platforms as well as utilized the newest high-tech instrumentation to manufacture your own MF device. 

Questions? 
Contact Dan Voicu at dan.voicu@utoronto.ca

title: NatureTO: Trees Around Taylor Memorial
description:
Taylor Memorial Branch and its neighbourhood is home to a variety of trees. Join the City of Toronto Urban Forestry staff to explore the natural world on a local neighbourhood tour. Learn how to recognize different species and fun facts about their cultural and ecological importance.
Children under 12 must be accompanied by a parent/caregiver.
Registration is required
The tour will start and end at the Taylor Memorial meeting room and will be guided by the City of Toronto Urban Forestry staff. There may be uneven, unpaved surfaces along the route. Please dress and prepare accordingly for this outdoor program  (hats, sunscreen, water, comfortable shoes). This program takes place rain or shine. In the event of severe inclement weather, registrants will be notified of an alternative date.

title: Mangiare, Hike, Repeat
description:
These Boots Are Made for Hiking
**Ciao Bella!** For our first international trip of the year - we have are heading to ITALY to trekk the dolomites or hike and tour Italy.
**JULY 11 - July 19**
This works in two ways - 2 groups, 2 paths. Because not everyone wants to trekk for four days, and because we are a large group we always offer two ways to come with us, because well we just want you to experience the best trips and a lot of fun!

SO.....
1\. You can sign up for the Trekking portion \- 4 days\, 3 nights\, hut to hut on the full Val Di Fassa trail plus two day hikes on the Thursday and Friday in the dolomite region hiking
OR
2\. A 7 day tour where we experience day hikes\, and Italy's dolomite village life\. We will spending our time in the Dolomites and Venice for the 7 days enjoying day hikes and hitting iconic dolomite spots along with Venice night life and mountain night life\. We will have lunch at the refugio and either the beginning or the end we will hike with the trecking group\.

All details, such as the costs, itinerary, exact fly in and out cities and meetup points will be supplied in the zoom call below. From there those who commit to the trip are then moved to a whats app where we follow the nitty gritty details of everyones flight bookings, gear, and flag ongoing questions, and ensure you are well prepared and organized for this trip)

If you miss the zoom call you miss the trip.

description: The Repair Café at the CNIB GTA Community Hub runs from 11 AM to 2 PM. The primary focus of this event is on repairing accessibility devices such as Perkins braillers, white canes, electronic magnifiers, talking and braille watches, and sewing-related repairs. The Repair Café does not charge for repairs, it is free! We encourage individuals to RSVP in advance to secure priority for repairs, although walk-ins are also welcome. While the event primarily serves the blind and visually impaired community, we may accommodate individuals outside of this community based on availability and foot traffic. For further details or inquiries, please feel free to contact Dom at Dom.Chan@cnib.ca.

description:
Hiking Network
⭐️ **A GUIDED HIKING TOUR OF THE ITALIAN ALPS** ⭐️
(Includes most meals, 5 guided hikes and private round-trip trail shuttle service)

**July 25-31, 2026** • 7 Days / 6 Nights

**Difficulty level:** Beginner/ Intermediate (some hiking experience required)

• **Price:** From EUR 1,550.00 pp (about CAD $2,500)
Flight NOT incl.

**Max 17 participants**

• HIGHLIGHTS
Explore the towering mountain peaks, bright-green valleys and quaint villages of the **Dolomites** (UNESCO Heritage Site) in the **Trentino** region of Italy.
From **Val di Sole,** a central site that will allow you to easily reach the starting points of each day hike, you will experience excursions of great satisfaction and with significantly different environmental characteristics. You will explore the jagged peaks of the **Brent**a Dolomites and the tonalite-rock mountains of **Adamello**, and move on to the sunny southern side of the **Ortles-Cevedale** chain, a territory which falls mostly within the protected area of ​​the **Stelvio National Park**... AND MORE!

title: I Who Have Never Known Men - Jacqueline Harpman
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi everyone,

Our selection for July is short but mighty story, and I'm here for it. It has been rediscovered recently on BookTok and is being compared to books like Margaret Atwood’s *A Handmaid's Tale* and Octavia E Butler’s *Parable* series. Translated from French and published in 1995 then slipped into relative obscurity. The themes are intense but I'm told that the storytelling and the message are well worth it. If you're interested in learning more about the book's resurgence, check out this great [Guardian article](https://www.theguardian.com/books/2025/feb/01/i-who-have-never-known-men-lost-dystopia-new-readers-after-buzz-on-tiktok).

Book of the Month
*I Who Have Never Known Men* \- Jacqueline Harpman \(1995\)

From Goodreads, *I Who Have Never Known Men* is a story about a group of women imprisoned and guarded. The women have no memory of how they got there, no notion of time, and only a vague recollection of their lives before. What comes next is a story of a young woman's fight to uncover her past and make her own future. People are divided on the story's finer points, but just about everyone I've read has echoed [What Is Quinn Reading](https://www.whatisquinnreading.com/reviews/i-who-have-never-known-men-book-review)'s review, saying they're grateful for the read and will carry it with them. At approximately 190 pages, I'm glad you'all feel that we should dive in and investigate this kind of story.

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/B9NMnC2F). Join us and keep the conversation going.

Join us for an all day bike riding event from Burlington Go to Niagara Falls and back. Total length of ride is 100km, so obviously this is not a beginner ride.
Please ensure you are bike ready so take your bike out and start practicing in the spring to get yourself in good shape for this ride! I will post some practice rides starting in May and June
No commuter bikes please.
You will catch the go train nearest you which is $10. and take it to the Burlington Go station which we will all meet -time to be confirmed, and begin our ride from there.
Lunch will be in Niagara Falls. Ensure you bring power snacks and water with lots of electrolytes!
[https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53737914](https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53737914)

title: 2026 UpFRONT Festival of Indigenous Arts, Music & Culture
location: Berczy Park,35 Wellington St E, Toronto, ON M5E 1C6, Canada
description:
Announcing TO Live’s 2026 UpFRONT Festival of Indigenous Arts, Music & Culture, taking place from August 14–16, 2025.

UpFRONT is a weekend-long celebration of Indigenous talent from across Turtle Island and beyond, featuring three days of exceptional music, comedy, puppetry, free workshops, and community programming in the heart of Tkaronto. All programming is free and open to the public.

In association with the festival, TO Live will be installing a temporary outdoor stage and closing Scott Street from Front Street East to Scott Lane. This location will serve as one of two performance stages, showcasing Indigenous artists from across Canada at no cost to attendees. This will require the temporary closure of this section of Scott Street to motor vehicles. Front Street will remain open to ongoing traffic.

In addition, there will be a pedestrian Indigenous marketplace along Scott Street from Front Street to Wellington Street and throughout Berczy Park. This marketplace will feature Indigenous artisan vendors, food trucks, pop-up food tents. As part of this activation, Scott Street south of the public parking lot will also be closed to motor vehicles. Neither of the Public parking lots on Scott Street will be blocked.

Alongside the marketplace, the existing platform within Berczy Park will become a second performance stage to fully animate the park and surrounding area.

Street closures will commence at 12:00 a.m. on August 14, 2025, and remain in effect until 11:59 p.m. on August 16, 2025.

Programming hours will be approximately 12:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m. on August 14, and 10:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. on August 15 and 16.

TO Live welcomes the St. Lawrence community to this free and inclusive celebration of Indigenous arts and culture. Additional information will be added as it becomes available.

title: CNIB GTA Hub
location: CNIB GTA Community Hub – 1525 Yonge St, Toronto, ON M4T 1Z2, Canada
description: The Repair Café at the CNIB GTA Community Hub runs from 11 AM to 2 PM. The primary focus of this event is on repairing accessibility devices such as Perkins braillers, white canes, electronic magnifiers, talking and braille watches, and sewing-related repairs. The Repair Café does not charge for repairs, it is free! We encourage individuals to RSVP in advance to secure priority for repairs, although walk-ins are also welcome. While the event primarily serves the blind and visually impaired community, we may accommodate individuals outside of this community based on availability and foot traffic. For further details or inquiries, please feel free to contact Dom at Dom.Chan@cnib.ca.
